questions.question: What does it mean for $f\colon X\to\mathbb{R}$ to be bounded?
questions.explanation: Boundedness means one finite number controls every output magnitude: $|f(x)|\le M$ for all $x\in X$.
option_explanations: Equality $f(x)=M$ would make $f$ constant, much stronger than boundedness.
The bound restricts outputs, not the input domain; $X$ may be unbounded.
Monotonicity concerns ordering of outputs and does not prevent unbounded growth.
